title: Viruses in multi-scale ocean models: challenges and opportunities
abstract: While viruses affect the flow of elements and energy at a planet-wide scale through lysis , gene transfer , and metabolic reprogramming , viruses are yet to be included in planetary-scale models of ecosystem function and nutrient cycling . Here , we review recent advances incorporating viruses into ocean models and ask : what barriers remain ? To address these challenges , we argue for a new generation of ocean models that are fully representative of the multifaceted influences of viruses across scales of organization . we describe ways to achieve this by integration of existing models built across scales , from molecules to ecosystems and the Earth System . To accelerate these advances , we emphasize the need for systematic , intercalibrated datasets for diverse experimental virus-host systems , wider application of new technologies to monitor in situ viral infections , and new software to integrate models across scales . Resolution of viruses within multi-scale models will open the door to assessing current biological uncertainties related to the impact of viral infection on nutrient retention in the surface ocean , carbon sequestration to depth , and the sensitivity of these processes to climate change .

title: Deep Neural Strategies for Regularization Parameters Estimation and Image Parameterization in PET Reconstruction
abstract: Positron Emission Tomography ( PET ) is a functional imaging technique widely used in oncology , enabling quantitative analysis of radiopharmaceuticals distribution . The reconstruction of PET images from raw data is an ill-posed inverse problem that requires regularization due to intrinsic high noise level . As a result , image quality strongly depends on the regularization method and the choice of regularization parameters . Current methods used in clinics apply the same setting to all patients . In this thesis , we explore two deep learning-based strategies to adapt regularization automatically for each individual scan with the aim of getting optimal image quality . The first approach uses a supervised residual neural network to predict optimal parameters for an established regularization method directly from raw data . A simulation pipeline was developed to efficiently generate realistic PET datasets and corresponding optimal parameters , allowing to build the training database . The second approach leverages Implicit Neural Representations ( INRs ) , modeling the image as a continuous function represented by a cartesian coordinate-based network , which is optimized directly from raw data via a physics-informed loss . The second approach introduces regularization implicitly and does not require training data .

title: LP4P: Link Prediction over Annotated Knowledge Graphs with Four Patterns
abstract: Initially designed for Knowledge Graphs ( KG ) containing plain ( s , p , o ) triples , research on link prediction has evolved to address more complex structures such as hypergraphs , hyper-relational graphs , and bi-level graphs . evolved push link prediction to handle annotation patterns , where a triple is annotated with another ( t , p , t ) , or where triples are annotated with qualifiers ( t , p , o ) . However , each approach focuses on a single annotation pattern , and the case where a triple is annotated with a subject ( s , p , t ) has never been explored . In this paper , we propose LP4P , the first link prediction model capable of predicting entities in both plain triples and three annotation patterns . LP4P , the first link prediction model capable of predicting entities in both plain triples and three annotation patterns captures the information expressed in annotations through a four-pattern attention layer , and LP4P , the first link prediction model capable of predicting entities in both plain triples and three annotation patterns loss function further leverages the ontological information of KGs . Moreover , we built WD4P , an RDF KG derived from baseline datasets , which includes three annotation patterns . Extensive empirical evaluations demonstrate that LP4P , the first link prediction model capable of predicting entities in both plain triples and three annotation patterns outperforms relevant state-of-the-art models on knowledge graphs with three annotation patterns , and achieves comparable performance on standard benchmarks .

title: Hierarchical Data-enabled Predictive Control for Building Thermal Management
abstract: Building thermal management accounts for a significant share of global energy consumption . The application of Model Predictive Control ( MPC ) in Building thermal management remains limited by the complexity of modeling . Data-enabled Predictive Control ( DeePC ) , which replaces explicit models with data-driven trajectory predictions , offers a promising alternative . However , Data-enabled Predictive Control ( DeePC ) , which replaces explicit models with data-driven trajectory predictions , reliance on quasi-linear dynamics limits Data-enabled Predictive Control ( DeePC ) , which replaces explicit models with data-driven trajectory predictions , direct control of nonlinear HVAC actuators . This work proposes a hierarchical framework : Data-enabled Predictive Control ( DeePC ) , which replaces explicit models with data-driven trajectory predictions , optimizes thermal power allocation at the supervisory level , while decentralized PI controllers , tuned via the model-free Virtual Reference Feedback Tuning method , regulate power . Validated on the Building Optimization Testing Framework ( BOPTEST ) , this approach eliminates explicit modeling and achieves superior energy efficiency and comfort management compared to conventional resistance-capacitance model MPC .
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Hub location for waterborne transportation networks in the context of the physical internet
abstract: This dissertation addresses optimization models for the design of logistics networks under the emerging paradigm of the Physical Internet ( PI ) , with a focus on river-based and multimodal transportation . Building on hub location theory and network design , This dissertation extends classical formulations to better reflect the structural and operational features of real logistics systems . The first contribution introduces the Tree-of-Hub Location Problem with Stopovers , which allows intermediate stopovers along inter-hub routes . A mixed-integer linear programming model , strengthened by valid inequalities , demonstrates the cost and flexibility benefits of extends . The second contribution develops hub location models for multimodal networks combining rivers and roads , illustrated through a case study on Colombia ’s Magdalena River . The third contribution adapts liner shipping service network design to the the emerging paradigm of the Physical Internet ( PI ) context , adding set-partitioning constraints to capture modular and interoperable flows . To address scalability , a Large Neighborhood Search ( LNS ) metaheuristic is implemented , providing high-quality solutions for large instances .

title: LP-4P : Link Prediction over Annotated Knowledge Graphs with Four Patterns
abstract: Initially designed for Knowledge Graphs ( KG ) containing plain ( s , p , o ) triples , research on link prediction has evolved to address more complex structures such as hypergraphs , hyper-relational graphs , and bi-level graphs . evolved push link prediction to handle annotation patterns where a triple is annotated with another ( t , p , t ) , or where a triple is annotated with qualifiers ( t , p , o ) . However , each approach focuses on a single annotation pattern , and the case where a triple is annotated with a subject ( s , p , t ) has never been explored . In this paper , we propose LP4P , the first link prediction model capable of predicting entities in both plain triples and three annotation patterns . LP4P , the first link prediction model capable of predicting entities in both plain triples and three annotation patterns captures the information expressed in annotations through a four-pattern attention layer , and LP4P , the first link prediction model capable of predicting entities in both plain triples and three annotation patterns loss function further leverages the ontological information of KGs . Moreover , we built WD4P , an RDF KG derived from baseline datasets , which includes three annotation patterns . Extensive empirical evaluations demonstrate that LP4P , the first link prediction model capable of predicting entities in both plain triples and three annotation patterns outperforms relevant state-of-the-art models on knowledge graphs with three annotation patterns , and achieves comparable performance on standard benchmarks .
keywords: knowledge graph and prediction and machine learning

title: Towards Process Optimization by Leveraging Relationships Between Electrical Wafer Sorting and Complete-Line Statistical Process Control Data
abstract: In semiconductor manufacturing , Statistical Process Control ( SPC ) ensures that products meet the Electrical Wafer Sort ( EWS ) tests performed at the end of the manufacturing flow . In this work , we model the Electrical Wafer Sort ( EWS ) tests performed at the end of the manufacturing flow using inline Statistical Process Control ( SPC ) data from the Front-End-Of-Line ( FEOL ) to the Back-End-Of-Line ( BEOL ) . Statistical Process Control ( SPC ) data tend to be inherently sparse because measuring all wafers , lots , and products is both costly and can significantly impact the throughput . In contrast , EWS data is densely collected at the die level , offering high granularity . we propose to model the problem as a regression task to uncover interdependencies between Statistical Process Control ( SPC ) and EWS data at the lot level . By applying two learning strategies , mono-and multi-target , we demonstrate empirically that leveraging families of EWS tests enhances model performance . The performance and practical relevance of the approach are validated through numerical experiments on real-world industrial data .

title: Babel-formal: Translation of Proofs between Lean and Rocq
abstract: In this work , we investigate using proof terms ( the low-level representation of formal proofs ) as a pivot language for translating proof scripts between proof assistants and across tactic sets . Unlike direct proof translation , using does not require an aligned training corpus ; using only needs aligned context at inference time so that both systems elaborate comparable terms . we compare two strategies : ( 1 ) direct script-to-script translation with an off-the-shelf LLM ( GPT-5 ) , and ( 2 ) proof term translation , where an LLM turns a proof term into a proof script in the target language . we build a small benchmark of aligned sources ( 14 files , 117 lemmas ) across Lean and Rocq , and train models to map Lean and Rocq proof terms back to Lean and Rocq proof terms native proof scripts . we experiments show that proof term translation works for cross-assistant translation and for translation between tactic sets . proof term translation is complementary to using a SoTA off-the-shelf LLM for direct proof script translation ( combining both performs best ) , scales easily in terms of training data , and handles tactic-set translation better ( e.g. , vanilla Rocq → SSReflect ) .

title: Exploring the computational and psychological aspects of a human-centered decision-making process for nurse rostering
abstract: This thesis aims to integrate human-centered ethical aspects into nurse rostering . We argue that classical operations research approaches to nurse rostering , which fix objectives and constraints within a mathematical model , fail to capture the procedural rationality of human decision-makers and raise ethical issues of autonomy and responsibility . We propose a contextualized approach that draws on insights from occupational health and organizational justice . insights from occupational health and organizational justice help identify essential aspects related to well-being and fairness . We then design an interactive tool that enables decision-makers to iteratively adjust constraints and objectives , thereby exploring different trade-offs and reinforcing decision-makers autonomy . The implementation , based on an integer linear programming model , incorporates a catalog of additional constraints and provides recommendations drawn from the literature . An experiment with participants demonstrates progressive learning , improved efficiency , and a preserved sense of autonomy . This research thus highlights the importance of designing interactive and multidisciplinary tools to foster responsible decision-making that is better aligned with organizational needs .

title: Coupled vs. Decoupled Motion Planning for Four-Robotic Arm Manipulation in a Shared Workspace: An Empirical Study
abstract: Multi-robot manipulator systems are increasingly used in industrial settings for tasks like coordinated assembly and pick-and-place operations . In such shared workspaces , multiple robotic arms must plan collision-free motions that account for each other ’s movements . plan is computationally challenging , as the joint configuration space grows exponentially with the number of degrees of freedom ( DoF ) . We study motion planning for a four-arm industrial cell ( KUKA KR6 , KUKA KR10 , UR10 , UR5 ) operating in a shared workspace under ROS / Gazebo / MoveIt . We compare a coupled planner in a 24-DoF composite space using OMPL RRT-Connect against a decoupled pipeline that plans per arm and then time-coordinates trajectories with a Detect-and-Pause heuristic . a Detect-and-Pause heuristic discretizes a 24-DoF composite space into voxels , builds a spatio-temporal occupancy matrix , detects inter-arm conflicts in advance , and resolves inter-arm conflicts by pausing the robot with larger remaining execution time . To ensure a fair comparison , task allocation and grasp configurations are fixed across methods , and identical controller and planning parameters are used . Benchmarks span three clutter levels defined by minimum interobject distance dmin ∈{30,20,10}cm . We generate 10 randomized instances per level . Results show a decoupled pipeline that plans per arm and then time-coordinates trajectories with a Detect-and-Pause heuristic dominates : 100 % success at all clutter levels ( vs. ∼81.7 % for coupled ) , a −28.9 % reduction in median planning time on average , and −26.1 % median makespan on average . Gains are largest at 20 cm , where interactions are frequent . Results suggest that time-based coordination on fixed single-arm paths is a simple , robust , and scalable alternative to centralized planning for multi-arm manipulation in shared workspaces .

title: SW3T-IoT : Smart Water Monitoring Based on a Three-Tier IoT Architecture
abstract: The growing impacts of climate change on water resources demand innovative monitoring and management strategies . This paper presents SW3T-IoT , an innovative water monitoring system leveraging Internet of Things ( IoT ) technologies to enhance water resource management under dynamic conditions . SW3T-IoT , an innovative water monitoring system leveraging Internet of Things ( IoT ) technologies to enhance water resource management under dynamic conditions adopts a three-tier architecture — edge , fog , and cloud — integrating a custom-designed LoRa-WDS node optimized for low power consumption and long-term autonomous operation . edge , fog , and cloud collect real-time data on water level , flow , pressure , temperature , and quality from distribution networks and reservoirs . Data are locally processed at edge , then transferred to the cloud for advanced analysis and visualization . A Geographic Information System ( GIS ) enhances spatial awareness and decision-making . To ensure adaptability , SW3T-IoT , an innovative water monitoring system leveraging Internet of Things ( IoT ) technologies to enhance water resource management under dynamic conditions integrates a continual learning ( CL ) framework for Biochemical Oxygen Demand ( BOD ) forecasting . a continual learning ( CL ) framework for Biochemical Oxygen Demand ( BOD ) forecasting allows models to incrementally update with new environmental data without catastrophic forgetting , maintaining accuracy and robustness as water quality dynamics evolve . A hybrid CNN – BiLSTM – Attention model , reinforced with PER , AER , LwF , and EWC strategies , supports adaptive prediction and knowledge retention . SW3T-IoT , an innovative water monitoring system leveraging Internet of Things ( IoT ) technologies to enhance water resource management under dynamic conditions delivers intuitive dashboards for engineers and water managers , providing a holistic , scalable , and intelligent solution for sustainable water resource management .

title: Prediction Fairness with respect to Sensitive Networks
abstract: Algorithmic fairness is an important axis of ethical AI . We propose a novel approach to assess and mitigate the unfairness of classification models with respect to a given sensitive networks , such as social networks or professional networks . In this context , the fairness of a model correspond to the absence of correlation between the model predictions and the existence / absence of relations in a given sensitive networks , such as social networks or professional networks . We formalize criteria based on known concepts of group fairness using the assortativity coefficient , and We derive a regularization framework to mitigate the unfairness of a supervised model . Preliminary experiments on real-world case studies suggests that a regularization framework to mitigate the unfairness of a supervised model can be useful to explore the trade-off between accuracy and fairness . However , the use of GNN architectures may be required to find good compromises .

title: Design of Robust Multi-Robot Formations for Collaborative Localization and Navigation
abstract: This thesis focuses on the joint navigation of a heterogeneous aerial / terrestrial multi-robot system . The objective is to ensure accurate localization of a target robot by using inter-robot range measurements to reconstruct a target robot position . This thesis focuses on the optimal placement of collaborative robots around a target robot to be localized in the presence of measurement noise with heterogeneous standard deviations . A local robustness analysis is then performed on collaborative robots to assess collaborative robots sensitivity in the presence of positioning errors of collaborative robots . This allows us to state the necessary and sufficient conditions on collaborative robots in order to maximize collaborative robots robustness against positioning errors of collaborative robots . An experimental scenario is implemented and confirms the value of robust formations in the presence of positioning uncertainties . In addition , the experimental results highlight the importance of accurately estimating the standard deviation of UWB sensor noise to improve the accuracy of a target robot localization . Finally , a formation control architecture based on nonlinear predictive control is formulated and implemented experimentally . The cost function incorporates the necessary and sufficient conditions for optimality in order to maximize localization accuracy while ensuring obstacle avoidance and target robot tracking .

title: Load balancing in the mail sorting process: a case study at the French postal company La Poste
abstract: This paper investigates a load balancing problem within the context of postal sorting operations at La Poste , the French postal service . Faced with declining mail volumes , La Poste , the French postal service must reorganize La Poste , the French postal service processes to maintain service quality and operational efficiency . Mail sorting is modeled as a Simple Assembly Line Balancing Problem ( SALBP-2 ) , where mail items ( tasks ) are assigned to containers ( stations ) in a way that minimizes load imbalances while respecting precedence constraints . precedence constraints take the form of independent chains , as each mail route follows a fixed delivery sequence . We propose three resolution methods : an exact approach based on a Mixed Integer Linear Programming ( MILP ) formulation , a metaheuristic algorithm based on simulated annealing , and a fast heuristic designed for industrial deployment which exploits the precedence constraint structure for faster convergence . a metaheuristic algorithm based on simulated annealing and a fast heuristic designed for industrial deployment which exploits the precedence constraint structure for faster convergence are tested on academic and real-world datasets much larger than those commonly used in the literature . In order to use academic and real-world datasets much larger than those commonly used in the literature several times a day , the resolution method needs to be fast in terms of calculation time . Due to a fast heuristic designed for industrial deployment which exploits the precedence constraint structure for faster convergence strong performance and low computation time , a fast heuristic designed for industrial deployment which exploits the precedence constraint structure for faster convergence has been implemented on industrial platforms at La Poste , the French postal service and is now used daily .
keywords: precedence constraint structure for faster convergence

title: Event-Driven Adaptation in the Computing Continuum Using Software Variability
abstract: The computing continuum aggregates edge , fog , and cloud infrastructure layers , promising lower latencies and improved performance for data-driven applications . In this context , keeping servicelevel objectives ( SLOs ) is challenging due to fluctuations in resource capacities and network uncertainties . We present an adaptive runtime that manages software configuration parameters , application placement , and scaling at runtime to enforce SLOs . an adaptive runtime that manages software configuration parameters , application placement , and scaling at runtime aims to maintain a separation between developers and providers roles while providing performance estimations for previously unseen configurations . This paper describes the proposed architecture , event model , and preliminary results over the Grid'5000 testbed .

title: Local Computing vs. Cloud Computing: An Empirical Study of Energy Consumption
abstract: The dominance of Software-as-a-Service ( SaaS ) has raised sustainability concerns due to Software-as-a-Service ( SaaS ) reliance on centralized cloud infrastructure and increasing energy consumption . This paper investigates a core principle of the Local-First Software ( LoFi ) paradigm , local processing , as a potential alternative . Through a controlled empirical study using SeekTune , an open-source music recognition application , we compare the end-user device and server energy consumption and data usage of a local processing architecture against a traditional Software-as-a-Service ( SaaS ) model for a computationally intensive task . we results demonstrate that , while local processing consumes more energy on the client device , the combined energy cost of data transmission and server-side computation in the SaaS model often results in a larger total systemic footprint . For modern mobile devices , processing locally can be significantly more energy-efficient overall . Our results challenge the long-held assumption that cloud offloading is inherently superior , and position the local processing aspect of LoFi as a crucial consideration for sustainable software design .

title: An HMM-Based Behavior Analysis Approach for QoE in VR : A Case Study of QoL Assessment via Orientation and Mobility Test
abstract: Virtual Reality ( VR ) , as a leading form of immersive media , has rapidly expanded into various application domains , raising the need for standardized methods to evaluate Virtual Reality ( VR ) Quality of Experience ( QoE ) . An ongoing recommendation , ITU-T P.IXC , titled " Interactive test methods for subjective assessment of XR communications " , is currently under joint development by the Video Quality Experts Group Immersive Media Group ( VQEG-IMG ) and ITU-T Study Group 12 ( SG12 ) . One major challenge identified in this context is the insufficient attention paid to user behaviors during tasks , despite the increasing availability of behavioral data . Although such data are often collected , such data are rarely analyzed in depth . In this paper , we proposed a Hidden Markov Model ( HMM)-based behavior analysis approach . Using a VR-based Orientation and Mobility ( O&M ) test designed for Quality of Life ( QoL ) assessment-one of the promising applications of Virtual Reality ( VR )-we leveraged the collected behavioral data to model behavior patterns . we results demonstrate that a Hidden Markov Model ( HMM)-based behavior analysis approach can effectively extract behavior-aware features , highlighting the potential of integrating behavior analysis into QoL assessment frameworks . we believe this work provides valuable insights into incorporating behavioral metrics into immersive media QoE evaluation and contributes to the development of ITU-T P.IXC .

title: A model for Distributed Machine Learning
abstract: Nowadays , distributed machine learning has become essential , given the limitations of traditional centralized approaches that rely on central model training and data collection . Although distributed AI has proven efficient and adaptable in overcoming the limitations of traditional centralized approaches that rely on central model training and data collection , distributed AI still faces important challenges , especially in dynamic , heterogeneous , and resource-limited environments . To address important challenges , especially in dynamic , heterogeneous , and resource-limited environments , this paper discusses the main approaches and current limitations of distributed machine learning within the Cloud – Edge – IoT continuum ( CEI ) and highlights our ongoing work on integrating intelligent monitoring mechanisms as a necessary enhancement . intelligent monitoring mechanisms makes distributed learning more adaptive , efficient , and stable .

title: Dynamic graph learning algorithms for digital twins of network architectures
abstract: This thesis advances graph-aware Network Digital Twins for next-generation mobile networks by demonstrating that explicitly modeling infrastructure as graphs enables more adaptive , data-efficient , and scalable intelligence than conventional abstractions . Modern 5G/6 G systems are heterogeneous , dynamic , and tightly constrained by evolving topologies spanning edge , transport , and cloud domains . Traditional prediction and optimization pipelines degrade when faced with structural change , sparse data , or intertwined design decisions . We develop two complementary graph-centric frameworks addressing the twin pillars of a Network Digital Twin : predictive modeling and guided resource optimization . The first provides inductive cellular traffic prediction that generalizes to newly deployed sites , mitigates data scarcity , and transfers knowledge across environments without exhaustive retraining . The second offers a topology-aware resource allocation approach that jointly handles architectural and placement choices under operational constraints , improving solution quality and scalability . Together two complementary graph-centric frameworks addressing the twin pillars of a Network Digital Twin : predictive modeling and guided resource optimization illustrate a unifying premise : embedding topological relational structure at the core of learning and decision processes yields systems that remain robust as networks evolve , reduce adaptation cost , and better align with real deployment needs . The work positions graph-aware methods as a foundational paradigm for future autonomous network management .

title: Improving Social Determinants of Health Documentation in French EHRs Using Large Language Models
abstract: Social determinants of health ( SDoH ) significantly influence health outcomes , shaping disease progression , treatment adherence , and health disparities . However , Social determinants of health ( SDoH ) documentation in structured electronic health records ( EHRs ) is often incomplete or missing . This study presents an approach based on large language models ( LLMs ) for extracting 13 SDoH categories from French clinical notes . We trained Flan-T5-Large on annotated social history sections from clinical notes at Nantes University Hospital , France . We evaluated Flan-T5-Large at two levels : ( i ) identification of SDoH categories and associated values , and ( ii ) extraction of detailed SDoH with associated temporal and quantitative information . The model performance was assessed across four datasets , including two that We publicly release as open resources . Flan-T5-Large achieved strong performance for identifying well-documented categories such as living condition , marital status , descendants , job , tobacco , and alcohol use ( F1 score > 0.80 ) . Performance was lower for categories with limited training data or highly variable expressions , such as employment status , housing , physical activity , income , and education . Flan-T5-Large identified 95.8 % of patients with at least one SDoH , compared to 2.8 % for ICD-10 codes from structured EHR data . We error analysis showed that performance limitations were linked to annotation inconsistencies , reliance on English-centric tokenizer , and reduced generalizability due to Flan-T5-Large being trained on social history sections only . These results demonstrate the effectiveness of NLP in improving the completeness of real-world SDoH data in a non-English EHR system .

title: Kinematic and static analyses of the spherical X-joint: a new cable-driven spherical 4R linkage
abstract: This work presents the spherical X-joint , a novel 4R spherical linkage featuring two pairs of identical links arranged in a crossed configuration . A rigorous kinematic analysis reveals that the spherical X-joint , a novel 4R spherical linkage featuring two pairs of identical links arranged in a crossed configuration exhibits a unique reflective symmetry and that the spherical X-joint , a novel 4R spherical linkage featuring two pairs of identical links arranged in a crossed configuration full-cycle mobility is theoretically equivalent to pure rolling between identical elliptical cones . This insight enables an unconstrained single-parameter description of the spherical X-joint , a novel 4R spherical linkage featuring two pairs of identical links arranged in a crossed configuration motion that extends a unique reflective symmetry to the mathematical analysis also . Such a description provides a compact and efficient kinematic and static model for the spherical X-joint , a novel 4R spherical linkage featuring two pairs of identical links arranged in a crossed configuration . Furthermore , a remote actuation strategy based on antagonistic cables is proposed , and it is analytically proven that the spherical X-joint , a novel 4R spherical linkage featuring two pairs of identical links arranged in a crossed configuration exhibits positive coactivation across the spherical X-joint , a novel 4R spherical linkage featuring two pairs of identical links arranged in a crossed configuration workspace . These findings demonstrate the spherical X-joint , a novel 4R spherical linkage featuring two pairs of identical links arranged in a crossed configuration strong potential for remote actuation applications , particularly in the design of lightweight , bio-inspired robotic wrists and manipulators .

title: Cooperative UAV Fleet based on Wireless Communication, a Flocking Perspective
abstract: Compared to a single Unmanned Aerial Vehicle ( UAV ) , deploying a coordinated fleet of UAVs can offer increased speed , flexibility , and robustness during complex missions . A central challenge in such multi-UAV systems lies in communication , which is often essential for cooperation and coordination . Ad-hoc networking combined with distributed control techniques seems a promising solution , enabling fully autonomous , scalable and fault-tolerant multi-UAV systems , known as Flying Ad-hoc Network ( FANET ) . Yet , despite intensive research efforts , the interplay between communication and control in FANETs remains insufficiently understood . In this thesis , we study the mutual influence of communication and multi-robot control algorithms , with the underlying goal of improving the coordination of UAV fleets . we focus on flocking , a distributed multi-robot control method that scales well , ensures collision avoidance and connectivity , and is well suited to micro-UAVs and ad-hoc Wi-Fi networks , two central technologies of this thesis . While flocking is a widely studied swarm strategy , flocking behavior under imperfect communication remains largely unexplored . The first contribution presented in this thesis is DANCERS , a robotic and network co-simulator tailored for the study of FANETs . DANCERS , a robotic and network co-simulator tailored for the study of FANETs is a flexible simulation framework able to synchronize any robotic simulator with any network simulator . Using DANCERS , a robotic and network co-simulator tailored for the study of FANETs and real-world experimentation , we demonstrate how communication constraints can severely perturb UAV control quality . we begin by studying the impact of network congestion on remote-controlled UAVs , and translate the lessons learned to flocking control , in order to analyze flocking control robustness under varying communication conditions . Finally , leveraging UAV mobility as a resource instead of a constraint , we introduce a novel algorithm for the deployment of aerial relay chains and trees . In a novel algorithm for the deployment of aerial relay chains and trees , a fleet autonomously forms a reconfigurable and extensible network that can provide real-time communication from remote and difficult-to-reach areas , enabling search-and-rescue and multi-target monitoring applications . a novel algorithm for the deployment of aerial relay chains and trees is evaluated in simulation using DANCERS , a robotic and network co-simulator tailored for the study of FANETs .

title: Spatial-aware Graph-based Representations for EEG Signal Classification
abstract: Functional connectivity , estimated from electroencephalography ( EEG ) , is a useful tool for analyzing neural activity due to Functional connectivity , estimated from electroencephalography ( EEG ) high temporal resolution and non-invasive nature . Modeling EEG signals using graphs has emerged as a promising approach ; however , most existing studies still overlook the electrode spatial configuration in graph construction . This thesis aims to develop graph-based representations for the classification of functional connectivity from EEG signals . The originality of the proposed approaches lies in the joint integration of electrode spatial arrangement and connectivity patterns . the proposed approaches are applied to the classification of mental workload and motor imagery within brain – computer interface ( BCI ) systems . More specifically , we propose : ( i ) an image-based representation of functional connectivity that incorporates electrode position , degree , and connectivity , enabling classification with convolutional neural networks ( CNNs ) ; ( ii ) a vector-based representation grounded in attractive and repulsive forces between electrodes , combined with classical classifiers such as support vector machines ( SVM ) ; and ( iii ) the exploration of various graph types classified with graph neural network ( GNN ) , leveraging spatial information and different distance measures , to identify the most suitable graph representation for such models .

title: Comparing Modelling and Simulation Tools in Order to Face a Manufacturing-System Contest
abstract: Modern systems require effective modelling and simulation techniques for accurate analysis and informed decision making . Various approaches exist in order to tackle discrete event systems such as ( i ) formal methods e.g. automata or Petri Nets ( PNs ) , which provide a formal graphical modelling approach [ GK21 ] with formal proof of properties , ( ii ) numerical approaches e.g. the dioid algebraic framework [ BRHB13 ] for analytical computations and performance evaluation ( iii ) and Discrete-Event Systems ( DESs ) simulation , to represent and simulate system behaviours over time [ BW10 ] and enable to compute samples properties . While they all serve to model and analyse systems , they all differ in the modelling process , abstraction level and output focus , making it difficult to determine which approach is the most suitable for the given requirements . This study compares they all strengths and limitations using the Flexibac system of the contest called IMIC [ KHBDC24 ] as our study case . Choosing a benchmark case is beneficial for comparing with others . This poster summary focuses specifically on the comparative insights derived from that experimental framework .

title: Mixed Signals: A Diverse Point Cloud Dataset for Heterogeneous LiDAR V2X Collaboration
abstract: Vehicle-to-everything ( V2X ) collaborative perception has emerged as a promising solution to address the limitations of single-vehicle perception systems . However , existing V2X datasets are limited in scope , diversity , and quality . To address these gaps , we present \ours { } , a comprehensive V2X dataset featuring 45.1k point clouds and 240.6k bounding boxes collected from three connected autonomous vehicles ( CAVs ) equipped with two different configurations of LiDAR sensors , plus a roadside unit with dual LiDARs . we dataset provides point clouds and bounding box annotations across 10 classes , ensuring reliable data for perception training . we provide detailed statistical analysis on the quality of Our dataset and extensively benchmark existing V2X methods on Our dataset . \ours { } is \textbf{ready-to-use } , with precise alignment and consistent annotations across time and viewpoints . we hope we work advances research in the emerging , impactful field of V2X perception . title: Improving Vulnerable Road-Users Detection through Hybrid Collaborative Perception and Detection Refinement
abstract: Ensuring the safety of autonomous vehicles in complex urban environments critically depends on accurate 3D object detection . While LiDAR sensors provide reliable depth information , LiDAR sensors effectiveness is limited by sparsity at long distances and occlusions , particularly in intersection scenarios . Collaborative perception addresses these challenges by enabling information sharing among vehicles and infrastructure sensors , with intermediate fusion offering a balance between communication efficiency and detection accuracy . However , existing collaborative perception frameworks exhibit a notable performance gap between detecting vehicles and vulnerable road users such as cyclists and pedestrians . In this work , we propose a novel hybrid collaboration framework designed to reduce a notable performance gap between detecting vehicles and vulnerable road users such as cyclists and pedestrians . a novel hybrid collaboration framework designed to reduce this gap leverages late-stage information from communicating agents to augment the ego agent 's point cloud , then applies a standard intermediate fusion strategy , followed by a refinement stage that further improves the detection accuracy of various objects . Experiments on the Mixed Signals dataset demonstrate that a novel hybrid collaboration framework designed to reduce this gap sets a new state-of-the-art in the detection of vulnerable road users in urban V2X scenarios

title: Time-To-Collision Constrained NMPC for Connected and Autonomous Vehicles
abstract: This paper presents a Time-to-Collision ( TTC ) constrained Nonlinear Model Predictive Control ( NMPC ) framework for Connected and Autonomous Vehicles ( CAVs ) navigating in dynamic urban environments . The proposed method integrates V2X ( Vehicle-to-Everything ) communication and probabilistic obstacle modeling to enhance safety and reactivity in the presence of uncertain dynamic obstacles . Trajectories communicated by CAVs are directly incorporated into the NMPC optimization loop , while non-connected agents are modeled with uncertainty-aware predictions . The controller incorporates both geometric and time-based safety constraints , notably through TTC metrics and confidence ellipses . We validate We approach through a series of Hardware-in-the-Loop ( HIL ) real-world experiments using ROSBOT 2R platforms within a centralized ROS2 architecture .

title: An AI-Based Sensorless Force Feedback in Robot-Assisted Minimally Invasive Surgery
abstract: ( 1 ) Background : Most robotic MIS platforms lack native haptic feedback , leaving surgeons to infer tissue loads from vision alone — an especially risky limitation in esophageal procedures . ( 2 ) Methods : We develop a sensorless , image-only force-estimation pipeline that maps endoscopic video to tool – tissue forces using a lightweight EfficientNetV2B0 CNN . a sensorless , image-only force-estimation pipeline that maps endoscopic video to tool – tissue forces using a lightweight EfficientNetV2B0 CNN is trained on 9691 labeled frames from in vitro esophageal experiments and validated against an FT300 load cell . For intraoperative feasibility , a sensorless , image-only force-estimation pipeline that maps endoscopic video to tool – tissue forces using a lightweight EfficientNetV2B0 CNN is deployed as a plug-in on PARA-SILSROB , consuming the existing laparoscope feed and driving a commercial haptic device . The runtime processes every 10th frame of a 60 FPS stream ( ≈6 Hz updates ) with ~15–20 ms per-prediction latency . ( 3 ) Results : On held-out tests , a sensorless , image-only force-estimation pipeline that maps endoscopic video to tool – tissue forces using a lightweight EfficientNetV2B0 CNN achieves MAE = 0.017 N and MSE = 0.0004 N2 , outperforming a recurrent CNN baseline while maintaining real-time performance on commodity hardware . Integrated evaluations confirm stable operation at the deployed update rate and low latency compatible with closed-loop haptics . ( 4 ) Conclusions : By avoiding distal force sensors and preserving sterile workflow , the approach is readily translatable and retrofit-friendly for current robotic platforms . The results support the practical feasibility of real-time , sensorless force feedback for robotic esophagectomy and related MIS tasks , with potential to reduce tissue trauma and enhance operative safety .

title: Coercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals for regular infinite-dimensional systems and applications
abstract: This paper proposes a procedure for constructing a coercive ISS-Lyapunov functional for regular infinite-dimensional systems that are exponentially stable . Indeed , as already known , Lyapunov functionals for infinite-dimensional systems does not need to be \color{black } coercive . Under the assumption that there exists an exactly observable output , we are able to modify any non-coercive Lyapunov functional into a coercive one . We also discuss the potential applications of such a Lyapunov functional in singular perturbation theory and output regulation . The results are illustrated on a non-trivial equation , namely , a linearized version of the Korteweg-de Vries equation .

title: LLM as a Guide: an Approach for Unsupervised Economic Relation Discovery in Administrative Documents
abstract: Effective relation extraction ( RE ) from unstructured text is critical , especially when the target relations are unknown . In this case , we can leverage Large Language Models ( LLMs ) to perform Effective relation extraction ( RE ) from unstructured text . In this paper , we present an LLM as a guide approach for identifying economic relations . This novel methodology , based on sentence clustering and an LLM , is used to identify previously unknown economic relations in French administrative documents . This novel methodology , based on sentence clustering and an LLM addresses the challenge of extracting actionable knowledge without predefined relation labels . we evaluate we approach on French and English RE datasets , demonstrating high precision and recall in detecting previously unknown relations . we results suggest that clustering and LLM-based methods can effectively discover and categorize economic relations , with potential applications to private corpora .

title: Invited Paper: On the Equivalence of Snapshot/Append Objects and Broadcast Abstractions under Byzantine Failures
abstract: Abstractions play a central role in distributed computing , as Abstractions capture essential synchronization properties . Equivalence results among abstractions clarify abstractions relative computational power . While many such equivalences are well established in crash-prone systems , far less is known about Byzantine-prone environments , where faulty processes may behave arbitrarily . This paper revisits the equivalence landscape in Byzantine systems , with a particular focus on shared registers and broadcast abstractions . We establish three new reductions . Specifically , We prove that the broadcast abstraction called Byzantine Set-Constrained Delivery Broadcast ( BSCD-Broadcast ) can implement a Snapshot / Append object and vice versa ( I.e. , a two-way reduction ) , and that the FIFO variant of the renowned Byzantine Reliable Broadcast ( BRB-Broadcast ) can implement the broadcast abstraction called Byzantine Set-Constrained Delivery Broadcast ( BSCD-Broadcast ) under a majority of correct processes . Interestingly , this assumption mirrors the one required in crash-prone systems for a similar transformation .

title: An abstract setting for the Fredholm backstepping transformation: self-adjoint case
abstract: In this paper we address the existence of a Fredholm backstepping transformation for self-adjoint operators A. we prove , under assumptions on the control operator B and A , that there exists a Fredholm backstepping transformation for operators A of order strictly greater than 1 . One of the main contribution of this paper is to exhibit the underlying isomorphism used to construct T . the underlying isomorphism used to construct T allows to deduce sharp estimates on ∥T ∥ L(H;H ) and ∥T-1 ∥ L(H;H ) with respect to the damping parameter λ > 0 . sharp estimates on ∥T ∥ L(H;H ) and ∥T-1 ∥ L(H;H ) with respect to the damping parameter λ > 0 allow we to prove the finite-time stabilization for a large class of self-adjoint operators .

title: Towards Scalable O-RAN Resource Management: Graph-Augmented Proximal Policy Optimization
abstract: Open Radio Access Network ( O-RAN ) architectures enable flexible , scalable , and cost-efficient mobile networks by disaggregating and virtualizing baseband functions . However , this flexibility introduces significant challenges for resource management , requiring joint optimization of functional split selection and virtualized unit placement under dynamic demands and complex topologies . Existing solutions often address functional split selection and virtualized unit placement under dynamic demands and complex topologies separately or lack scalability in large and real-world scenarios . In this work , we propose a novel Graph-Augmented Proximal Policy Optimization ( GPPO ) framework that leverages Graph Neural Networks ( GNNs ) for topology-aware feature extraction and integrates action masking to efficiently navigate the combinatorial decision space . we approach jointly optimizes functional split and placement decisions , capturing the full complexity of O-RAN resource allocation . Extensive experiments on both small-and large-scale O-RAN scenarios demonstrate that Our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines , achieving up to 18 % lower deployment cost and 25 % higher reward in generalization tests , while maintaining perfect reliability . These results highlight the effectiveness and scalability of Our approach for practical O-RAN deployments .

title: An intelligent data-driven model for sustainable-resilient supplier scrutiny and selection in sustainable reconfigurable manufacturing systems
abstract: In the research stream of sustainable reconfigurable manufacturing systems , sustainable and resilient supplier scrutiny and selection emerges as a key strategy , emphasising the imperative of integrating sustainability and resiliency into the supply chain fabric . sustainable and resilient supplier scrutiny and selection extends beyond mere economic evaluations by incorporating environmental stewardship , social responsibility , and resilience against disruptions into the supplier assessment processes . While studies in these fields have made significant strides , there remains a scarcity of research investigating and providing performance appraisal approaches for sustainable-resilient suppliers within such systems . Motivated by addressing the recognised gap , this study aims to identify key criteria for scrutinising sustainable-resilient suppliers through a state-of-the-art review and develop an intelligent data-driven model that incorporates fuzzy logic to effectively navigate uncertainties , leveraging AI-based capabilities to enhance supplier scrutiny and selection in complex systems . To this end , this study presents an illustrative case to demonstrate the practical configuration of an intelligent data-driven model that incorporates fuzzy logic to effectively navigate uncertainties , leveraging AI-based capabilities to enhance supplier scrutiny and selection in complex systems as well as a case study to corroborate an intelligent data-driven model that incorporates fuzzy logic to effectively navigate uncertainties , leveraging AI-based capabilities to enhance supplier scrutiny and selection in complex systems validity . The case studies confirmed that an intelligent data-driven model that incorporates fuzzy logic to effectively navigate uncertainties , leveraging AI-based capabilities to enhance supplier scrutiny and selection in complex systems effectively assesses sustainable-resilient suppliers , improving precision and execution time while providing insights for informed decision-making through an intelligent data-driven model that incorporates fuzzy logic to effectively navigate uncertainties , leveraging AI-based capabilities to enhance supplier scrutiny and selection in complex systems analytical depth and computational efficiency . Furthermore , sensitivity analysis and sensitivity analysis integration into an intelligent data-driven model that incorporates fuzzy logic to effectively navigate uncertainties , leveraging AI-based capabilities to enhance supplier scrutiny and selection in complex systems are discussed .

title: Modeling OCL Collection Types and Type Casting using Constraint Programming
abstract: In Model-Driven Engineering ( MDE ) , the Unified Modeling Language ( UML ) is often combined with the Object Constraint Language ( OCL ) to express constraints on models . While constraints on models are typically used for validation , certain tasks-such as model search , completion , repair , or explorationrequire the automatic generation of models that satisfy certain tasks-such as model search , completion , repair , or explorationrequire . Due to the combinatorial nature of certain tasks-such as model search , completion , repair , or explorationrequire , even small models can lead to computationally complex problems . Constraint Programming ( CP ) offers a powerful paradigm for modeling and solving such combinatorial challenges , notably through the use of global constraints , which enable concise models supported by efficient algorithms . Although previous approaches have tackled model search using tools like Alloy or ATLc , previous approaches often rely on simplified subsets or avoid the use of global constraints . In this paper , we extend the ATLc approach by leveraging Constraint Programming ( CP ) to the expressiveness and coverage of the Unified Modeling Language ( UML ) . we introduce a Constraint Programming ( CP ) model for representing the Unified Modeling Language ( UML ) instances and evaluating queries , along with global constraint formulations for the Unified Modeling Language ( UML ) collection types ( Sequence , Bag , Set , OrderedSet ) and UML collection types ( Sequence , Bag , Set , OrderedSet ) corresponding the Object Constraint Language ( OCL ) casting operations ( asSequence , asBag , asSet and asOrderedSet ) . Finally we provide an implementation allowing we to test we model for this subset of the Object Constraint Language ( OCL ) and compare with related work .

title: Embodiment Curve: a Graphical Method to Visualize the Temporal Evolution of the Sense of Embodiment in VR
abstract: The Sense of Embodiment ( SoE ) in VR is a psychological state which naturally fluctuates over time . Embodiment questionnaires are commonly used in research as assessment tools . Yet , Embodiment questionnaires inherently limit the range of expression and are ill-suited to capture the temporal dynamics of embodied experiences . Building on the UX curve method used in user experience research , we propose the Embodiment Curve method . we conducted a user study with 12 participants in VR , who embodied an avatar to complete four tasks in a virtual hair salon . we assessed 12 participants in VR , who embodied an avatar to complete four tasks in a virtual hair salon SoE using both the Embodiment Curve and a classical embodiment questionnaire . the Embodiment Curve shows the temporality of the embodiment . we observed two distinct drawing strategies for constructing the Embodiment Curve : task-oriented or trend-oriented . A majority of participants preferred the Embodiment Curve due to the Embodiment Curve task-by-task form and the Embodiment Curve freedom . Moreover , the Embodiment Curve facilitates the verbalization of their SoE the Embodiment Curve thus appears to be a promising qualitative method for studying their SoE

title: Listening is Better Understood with: Minds, Milieux, Machines and; Musics
abstract: This paper proposes a conceptual framework for understanding listening as a four-way interaction in-and-between minds , milieux , machines , and musics . Building on cognitive , ecological , computational , and cultural approaches to sound , we explore how each of minds , milieux , machines , and musics contributes uniquely to auditory experience and interpretation . minds bring perceptual , cognitive , and emotional grounding ; milieux provide ecological and sociocultural contexts ; machines offer tools for sensing , modeling , and synthesis in sonic environments ; and musics embody structured forms of human expression and shared aesthetic meanings . Through pairwise and three-way analyses , we identify the pitfalls of excluding any one component — leading to disembodiment , inefficiency , or cultural disconnection . We advocate for a transdisciplinary synthesis that situates listening within networks of perception , technology , and environment . We goal is to recenter listening as a reflexive , situated , and multiscalar practice across disciplines .

title: Fraw: Sampling-Based Approximate Query Processing for Federations of SPARQL Endpoints
abstract: SPARQL federation engines allow users to query multiple SPARQL endpoints as if all RDF data were available through a single virtual endpoint . However , executing complex SPARQL queries over federations while maintaining fast response times remains a major challenge . In this demonstration , we present Fraw , a SPARQL federation engine that supports sampling-based approximate query processing . sampling-based approximate query processing is particularly useful in scenarios where response time is essential and approximate results are acceptable . we showcase the effectiveness of Fraw , a SPARQL federation engine that supports sampling-based approximate query processing through an interactive SPARQL query autocompletion use case , where users receive timely suggestions during query authoring , despite the complexity of federated querying .

title: Continuation Queries: Embracing Timeouts on Public SPARQL Endpoints
abstract: Public SPARQL endpoints , such as Wikidata , provide essential access points to large-scale knowledge graphs . However , Public SPARQL endpoints , such as Wikidata often suffer from strict timeouts that prevent the retrieval of complete query results . This demonstration presents the first public deployment of passage , a SPARQL query engine that guarantees query completeness through continuation queries . Instead of failing upon timeout , passage , a SPARQL query engine that guarantees query completeness through continuation queries returns partial results along with a SPARQL continuation query capable of retrieving the missing results . a SPARQL continuation query capable of retrieving the missing results can be chained iteratively until complete results are obtained . For This demonstration , attendees can interact with a passage loaded with 13B triples from Wikidata , and observe in detail a passage loaded with 13B triples from Wikidata 2025 operation during attendees query execution .

title: Table-Text Alignment: Explaining Claim Verification Against Tables in Scientific Papers
abstract: Scientific claim verification against tables typically requires predicting whether a claim is supported or refuted given a table . However , we argue that predicting the final label alone is insufficient : predicting reveals little about the model ’s reasoning and offers limited interpretability . To address this , we reframe table – text alignment as an explanation task , requiring models to identify the table cells essential for claim verification . we build a new dataset by extending the SciTab benchmark with human-annotated cell-level rationales . Annotators verify the claim label and highlight the minimal set of cells needed to support Annotators decision . After the annotation process , we utilize the collected information and propose a taxonomy for handling ambiguous cases . we experiments show that ( i ) incorporating table alignment information improves claim verification performance , and ( ii ) most LLMs , while often predicting correct labels , fail to recover human-aligned rationales , suggesting that most LLMs predictions do not stem from faithful reasoning .

title: Bioacoustics on Tiny Hardware at the BioDCASE 2025 Challenge
abstract: The BioDCASE initiative aims to encourage the invention of methods for detection and classification of acoustic scenes and events ( DCASE ) within the domain of bioacoustics . We have contributed to the first edition of The BioDCASE initiative by means of a task named " bioacoustics on tiny hardware " . The motivation for a task named " bioacoustics on tiny hardware " resides in the growing need for operating bioacoustic event detection algorithms on low-power autonomous recording units ( ARU 's ) . Participants were tasked with developing a detector of bird vocalizations from the yellowhammer ( Emberiza citrinella ) , given two hours of audio as a training set . a detector of bird vocalizations from the yellowhammer ( Emberiza citrinella ) had to run within the resource constraints of an ESP32-S3 microcontroller unit . By evaluating the submitted models on a withheld dataset , We conducted an independent benchmark that assessed both classification performance and resource efficiency through multiple metrics : average precision , inference time , and memory usage . We reported results confirm that recent advances in " tiny machine learning " ( TinyML ) have transformative potential for computational bioacoustics . For more information , please visit : [ URL ]

title: Annotation Meta-Model for Collaboration among Health Professionals
abstract: Collaboration among Health Professionals ( HPs ) is a cornerstone of high-quality medical care . Collaboration among Health Professionals ( HPs ) success depends not only on the availability of clinical information but also on the effectiveness of information exchange . Electronic Health Records ( EHRs ) have become the central medium for storing and sharing patient data , yet current systems rarely capture the dynamics of professional interactions . capture reduces the potential of Electronic Health Records ( EHRs ) to fully support collaborative decision making and coordinated care . To address this gap , we propose an annotation-based approach aimed at enhancing collaboration within EHR environments . we contribution is threefold . First , we define methods to structure interactions by explicitly capturing who communicates what and when , thereby organizing the flow of exchanged information . Second , we introduce semantic enrichment techniques that add contextual and meaningful interpretation to annotations . Third , we design a meta-annotation model , grounded in a Knowledge-Based System ( KBS ) , that formally represents collaborative exchanges and ensures consistency . A software prototype operationalizes these concepts , providing a practical tool to support annotation creation and management . By bridging raw information with structured , semantically rich collaboration , an annotation-based approach aimed at enhancing collaboration within EHR environments enhances workflows , strengthens decision-making , and ultimately improves healthcare delivery .

title: A New vTPM Architecture with Strong Isolation for the Cloud
abstract: Cloud infrastructures often lack robust mechanisms for verifying the integrity of Virtual Machines ( VM ) , especially when the hypervisor or host Operating System ( OS ) are not fully trusted . Virtual Trusted Platform Modules ( vTPMs ) are widely used to support integrity measurement , but Virtual Trusted Platform Modules ( vTPMs ) reliance on the underlying infrastructure weakens Virtual Trusted Platform Modules ( vTPMs ) security guarantees . In this paper , we propose a secure vTPM architecture operating in an Intel SGX enclave . a secure vTPM architecture operating in an Intel SGX enclave offers strong isolation guarantees and enables integrity measurements to be performed independently of the host environment . we demonstrate how essential TPM functionalities , such as sealing , signing , and PCR operations , can be efficiently implemented and protected within an Intel SGX enclave . a secure vTPM architecture operating in an Intel SGX enclave also includes countermeasures against common attacks targeting vTPM , including NVRAM tampering , rollback attacks , cuckoo attacks , and unauthorized vTPM instantiation . Experimental results show that a secure vTPM architecture operating in an Intel SGX enclave offers corresponding solid security guarantees with minimal performance overhead . By decoupling trust from the host platform and anchoring trust in a Trusted Execution Environment ( TEE ) , this approach improves the reliability and security of vTPMs .

title: Towards Low-Latency Object Detection on Board Reactive Search-and-Rescue Drones
abstract: Drones play a crucial role in search-and-rescue missions by providing real-time information on areas of interest that are difficult to access or endangering to human rescuers . However , analyzing raw video feeds by human operators to detect objects of interest , such as vehicles or victims , becomes increasingly demanding as the mission duration increases . becomes underscores the need for embedded computer vision to reduce the operator 's cognitive load and enhance mission responsiveness . Towards this goal , we propose a low-latency object detection model based on YOLO , fitted to search-and-rescue missions , and able to process data coming from RGB and event cameras . we also propose a low-latency implementation on FPGA on board drones , achieving accurate detection in less than 20ms . Through a series of tests using a prototype drone , we highlight the features of the model and processing core that favor drone reactivity and operational autonomy .

title: A Classification Of The Triggers For The Co-Transformation Of Organizations Using A PLM Approach
abstract: Organizational and digital co-transformation projects are highly challenging and the current practices against these challenges are still limited in terms of efficiency and effectiveness . are is leading to the need of innovative decision supports to help managers conducting such strategies in optimal way . This paper presents a preliminary synthesis of the ongoing work aiming to define the first components of the framework that will be used to support organizational and digital co-transformation based on PLM and PPR approaches . This paper will focus on the definition of a PLM approach and describe the first components of the framework that will be used to support organizational and digital co-transformation based on PLM and PPR approaches .

title: Characterizing and managing known uncertainties in aircraft assembly
abstract: Aircraft assembly relies on the multi-mode resource-constrained project scheduling problem to coordinate complex tasks and resources under tight production targets . However , coordinate can be disrupted by unforeseen events such as missing parts , critical component shortages , late engineering changes , and unavailability of jigs and tools . unforeseen events such as missing parts , critical component shortages , late engineering changes , and unavailability of jigs and tools pose significant challenges to the assembly schedule . Missing or delayed parts can stall work-in-progress aircraft , leading to idle time and cascading delays , while late design changes often force out-of-sequence work and reassignment of resources . Such disturbances or disruptions undermine line balancing , lead times , and throughput , demanding dynamic readjustments by decision-makers to maintain milestones . This talk focuses on characterizing known uncertainties and takes a closer look at known uncertainties sources and the extent and ways in which known uncertainties affect internal manufacturing performance . We investigate how these events can spread through different layers of decision-making and result in last-minute changes . The main goal is to gain a better understanding of the impacts of such events and to identify the decisions and levers that can help mitigate such events both more easily and faster . A set of resilience ( reliability and responsiveness ) key performance indicators and strategies , designed to help aircraft assembly systems adapt swiftly and manage unexpected events , will be discussed and evaluated under normal and abnormal operating conditions . This contributes to supporting the dynamic readjustment of production plans , helping to ensure assembly continuity even in the face of unexpected events .
keywords: multi mode resource constrained project scheduling problem

title: FLAIR: Federated Learning with Adaptive and Intelligent Reasoning for Client Selection
abstract: The widespread adoption of the Internet of Things ( IoT ) in our technology-driven society raises significant security and privacy concerns , highlighting the need for collaborative Intrusion Detection Systems ( IDS ) that leverage Deep Learning ( DL ) methods to detect suspicious network traffic . Using both the computing power and local data available at distributed end devices , Federated Learning ( FL ) provides a decentralized learning paradigm that preserves data privacy . However , the system heterogeneity and the Independent and Identically Distributed ( non-IID ) distribution of FL clients ' data introduce various challenges that impact training efficiency . To address various challenges that impact training efficiency , we propose an adaptive approach named FLAIR , which leverages a semi-synchronous FL mechanism and a Decision Transformer ( DT ) to select clients that not only enhance the global model 's performance but also reduce communication and computation overhead . a Decision Transformer ( DT helps to make client selection decisions by considering both current and historical information , with the global model 's trained offline using various client selection policies . The process begins by generating an offline database , which will be used to train a Decision Transformer ( DT offline . Then , a Decision Transformer ( DT is deployed for online client selection under a semi-synchronous protocol , enabling a fully adaptive FL system . Extensive experiments on IDS datasets show that an adaptive approach named FLAIR , which leverages a semi-synchronous FL mechanism and a Decision Transformer ( DT ) significantly reduces computation and communication time by up to 94 % and 93 % , respectively , while maintaining comparable classification performance to the baseline models .

title: Development of an innovative parallel robot used in laparoscopic pancreatic surgery
abstract: This paper introduces the development and preliminary validation of a novel parallel robot specifically engineered for laparoscopic pancreatic surgeries . Parallel robots , unlike traditional serial robotic systems , provide superior stiffness , precision , and payload capacity , attributes that are crucial for delicate surgical procedures . This paper elaborates on the design of a novel parallel robot specifically engineered for laparoscopic pancreatic surgeries . Key objectives include expanding the operational field to facilitate better access to the pancreas and enhancing the efficiency of medical protocols . The design process is comprehensively detailed , starting from medical task parameters to the kinematic architecture and functional capabilities of a novel parallel robot specifically engineered for laparoscopic pancreatic surgeries . a novel parallel robot specifically engineered for laparoscopic pancreatic surgeries features a modular architecture comprising an active 3-degree-of-freedom parallel mechanism and a passive spherical parallel mechanism . a modular architecture comprising an active 3-degree-of-freedom parallel mechanism and a passive spherical parallel mechanism supports a new active surgical instrument with four degrees of freedom , significantly enhancing dexterity and enabling surgeons to access deep organs more effectively . To assess a novel parallel robot specifically engineered for laparoscopic pancreatic surgeries efficacy , a series of laboratory tests were conducted to simulate conditions typical of laparoscopic pancreatic surgeries . The results indicate substantial improvements in surgical maneuverability , precision , and ergonomic efficiency , underscoring a novel parallel robot specifically engineered for laparoscopic pancreatic surgeries potential to enhance surgical outcomes .

title: Two Arms, One Goal: Reproducible Dual-Arm Robotic Fruit Harvesting
abstract: Interest in agricultural robotics has significantly increased , due to the potential benefits of improved productivity and labor reduction . Yet , developing robotic harvesters for unstructured environments presents many challenges for robot perception , planning and action . Here , we propose a dual-arm approach to fruit harvesting . we dual-arm fruit harvesting robots are equipped with an RGB-D camera , a cutting and a collecting tool . The vision system combines fruit detection and tracking . we detect branches and the tree trunk as obstacles , to ensure efficient and safe harvesting . To speed up the process , we implement a scheduling algorithm based on the traveling salesperson problem ( TSP ) to minimize the distance required to harvest all visible fruits . Finally , we use global motion planning to ensure collision-free operation . we validate we methods using two distinct dual-arm robots : Baxter , a cost-effective and widely available option , and BAZAR , a custom high precision dualarm platform . Furthermore , we experiments are conducted on two types of fruit : apples and oranges . In lab trials , Our dual-arm fruit harvesting robots harvested 5 oranges and 6 apples , with average perfruit times of 20.6 s and 8.2 s and no collisions . Perception achieved mAP@50 = 0.886 on a 3,600-image dataset , MOTA = 89.8 % with 3 ID switches , and 3D localization MAE of 7.8-21.1 mm . The results demonstrate the effectiveness of a dual-arm approach to fruit harvesting increasing adaptability of robotic fruit harvesting . The results demonstrate the effectiveness of a dual-arm approach to fruit harvesting in enhancing the efficiency and adaptability of robotic fruit harvesting .

title: Kinematic Analysis of a Spherical Five-Bar Linkage Using Quaternions
abstract: Athena is a modular medical robot of which one module is a passive spherical 5-bar mechanism . Within this paper the complete kinematic analysis of the spherical 5-bar using quaternions will be provided . the complete kinematic analysis of the spherical 5-bar using quaternions includes forward and inverse kinematics as well as forward and inverse singularities in workspace and joint space .

title: Biomechanically consistent real-time action recognition for human-robot interaction
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for real-time human action recognition in industrial contexts , using standard 2D cameras . We introduce a complete pipeline for robust and real-time estimation of human joint kinematics , input to a temporally smoothed Transformer-based network , for action recognition . We rely on a new dataset including 11 subjects performing various actions , to evaluate We approach . Unlike most of the literature that relies on joint center positions ( JCP ) and is offline , We uses biomechanical prior , eg . joint angles , for fast and robust real-time recognition . Besides , joint angles make a novel framework for real-time human action recognition in industrial contexts , using standard 2D cameras agnostic to sensor and subject poses as well as to anthropometric differences , and ensure robustness across environments and subjects . We proposed learning model outperforms the best baseline model , running also in real-time , along various metrics . Our proposed learning model achieves 88 % accuracy and shows great generalization ability , for subjects not facing the cameras . Finally , We demonstrate the robustness and usefulness of a novel framework for real-time human action recognition in industrial contexts , using standard 2D cameras , through an online interaction experiment , with a simulated robot controlled in real-time via the recognized actions .

title: Impact of Heterogeneous UWB Sensor Noise on the Optimality and Sensitivity of Mobile Positioning Systems
abstract: In this paper , we propose a theoretical framework for designing a multi-robot formation equipped with Ultra-wideband ( UWB ) sensors to localize a target robot . In the presence of noisy range measurements , the accuracy of a target robot pose estimation is highly dependent on the chosen formation geometry . Different from existing works , we account for the heterogeneous standard deviations of range measurements across different UWB transmitter-receiver pairs . we establish new optimality conditions for formation geometries and conduct a sensitivity analysis of optimal formations under robot positioning errors . In a 2D setting , we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for both optimality and robustness to robot positioning uncertainty . Experimental results confirm the heterogeneous standard deviations of range measurements across different UWB transmitter-receiver pairs and validate a target robot confidence ellipse model . An experimental comparison of formation geometries , optimized with and without considering heterogeneous noise , emphasizes the importance of accounting for the heterogeneous standard deviations of range measurements across different UWB transmitter-receiver pairs . In addition , we experimentally demonstrate that robust formation geometries improve the target robot ’s confidence ellipse model in the presence of positioning errors .

title: Tactile-based force estimation for interaction control with robot fingers
abstract: Fine dexterous manipulation requires reactive control based on rich sensing of manipulator-object interactions . Tactile sensing arrays provide rich contact information across the manipulator ’s surface . However Tactile sensing arrays implementation faces two main challenges : accurate force estimation across complex surfaces like robotic hands , and integration of these estimates into reactive control loops . We present a data-efficient calibration method that enables rapid , full-array force estimation across varying geometries , providing online feedback that accounts for non-linearities and deformation effects . We force estimation model serves as feedback in an online closed-loop control system for interaction force tracking . The accuracy of We estimates is independently validated against measurements from a calibrated force-torque sensor . Using the Allegro Hand equipped with Xela uSkin sensors , We demonstrate precise force application through an admittance control loop running at 100Hz , achieving up to 0.12±0.08 [ N ] error margin — results that show promising potential for dexterous manipulation .
keywords: tactile sensing sensor arrays interaction force estimation and control robotic hands
