title: 3D Data Practices and Preservation for Humanities: A Decade of the Consortium “3D for Digital Humanities”
abstract: For more than a decade ( 2014–2025 ) , the Consortium “ 3D for Digital Humanities ” has been advancing the use of 3D technologies in the Humanities and Social Sciences ( HSS ) while structuring and supporting the research community . the Consortium “ 3D for Digital Humanities ” now brings together more than 30 teams , primarily from academic research , but also increasingly from the cultural sector . Under the Consortium “ 3D for Digital Humanities ” coordination , significant achievements have been realized , including best-practice guides , an infrastructure for the publication of 3D data , and dedicated software for documentation , dissemination , and archiving , as well as a metadata schema , all fully aligned with FAIR principles . the Consortium “ 3D for Digital Humanities ” has developed national training programs , particularly on metadata and ethical practices , and contributed to important initiatives such as the reconstruction of Notre-Dame de Paris , while actively engaging in European projects . the Consortium “ 3D for Digital Humanities ” has also fostered international collaborations to broaden perspectives , share methodologies , and amplify impacts . Looking ahead ( 2025–2033 ) , the Consortium “ 3D for Digital Humanities ” aims to address the environmental impact of 3D data production and storage by proposing best practices for digital sustainability and efficiency . the Consortium “ 3D for Digital Humanities ” is also expanding the National 3D Data Repository , enhancing interoperability , and adopting emerging standards to meet evolving scientific needs . Building on the Consortium “ 3D for Digital Humanities ” past achievements , the Consortium “ 3D for Digital Humanities ” intends to further advance 3D research and 3D research applications across disciplines , positioning 3D data as a key component of future scientific data clouds .

title: Extracting and clustering human visual strategies from video gaze data with hidden markov models for video-QA performance understanding
abstract: Human gaze patterns during tasked viewing of an action offer insights into human attention , intention recognition , and the cognitive state of the viewer . insights into human attention , intention recognition , and the cognitive state of the viewer have applications in many domains such as collaborative robotics , user interface design , and medical assessment . In this work , we demonstrate an association between visual strategies employed during task-driven viewing and performance in video question answering ( Video-QA ) . To do so , we leverage eye-tracking data to analyze human visual strategies during action recognition . Specifically , we record participants ' gaze as participants ' watch demonstrations of short atomic actions , which form a basis to describe all long form actions , followed by a questionanswering step to assess participants ' comprehension . we model the spatio-temporal dynamics of gaze behavior using Hidden Markov Models ( HMMs ) and cluster visual strategies for demonstrations of the same task based on visual behavior similarity . we use Binomial Generalized Linear Mixed Model ( BGLMM ) to investigate how gaze behavior relates to Video-QA performance . we results show that participants who exhibit specific visual strategies , as well as participants who are consistent in their visual strategy across different videos , perform better on the same task , while other visual strategies are associated with poor performance and can reveal misunderstandings of the questions . Specifically , more dynamic gaze behavior , with more focused fixations on a relevant object , and more relevant objects considered in the scene are all properties of a better performing visual strategy . By identifying gaze patterns associated with Video-QA performance , using a probabilistic Bayesian method with interpretable learnable parameters , we approach enables clearer insights into human perception , potentially contributing to more robust and efficient action recognition machine learning models .

title: Behavior Metric for Evaluating the Impact of Visual Distortions on User Viewport in a VR Navigation Experience
abstract: Visual distortions significantly impact user experience in virtual reality ( VR ) . Understanding impact is essential for delivering a higher-quality VR experience . However , existing studies focus on distortions from image capturing , processing , or display , relying largely on self-reported scores . The impact of visual distortions on viewport caused by simulated visual impairments in VR remains underexplored , despite The impact of visual distortions on viewport caused by simulated visual impairments in VR importance in creating realistic VR experiences , raising public awareness , and studying the effects of visual impairment . This study proposes a Hidden Markov Model ( HMM)-based behavior entropy metric to measure the effects of visual distortions on a user 's viewport in a 6-Degrees-of-Freedom ( DoF ) VR navigation experience . An Orientation and Mobility ( O&M ) VR scenario designed to assess the navigation performance of visually impaired individuals was used for This study . Results reveal a relationship between behavior entropy and distortion severity : slight to moderate distortions reduce entropy , while severe distortions cause a significant decline . Additionally , behavior entropy correlates with O&M test performance metrics , indicating behavior entropy potential as an objective behavioral measure of VR navigation performance . Results highlight the value of behavior analysis in evaluating VR user experience , offering a new analytical perspective on visual distortion effects and expanding applications of behavior analysis in multidisciplinary research .

title: Multi-Class-Token Transformer for Multitask Self-supervised Music Information Retrieval
abstract: Contrastive learning and equivariant learning are effective methods for self-supervised learning ( SSL ) for audio content analysis . Yet , Contrastive learning and equivariant learning application to music information retrieval ( MIR ) faces a dilemma : Contrastive learning is more effective on tagging ( e.g. , instrument recognition ) but less effective on structured prediction ( e.g. , tonality estimation ) ; equivariant learning can match supervised methods on the specific task equivariant learning is designed for , but equivariant learning does not generalize well to other tasks . In this article , we adopt a best-of-both-worlds approach by training a deep neural network on both kinds of pretext tasks at once . The proposed new architecture is a Vision Transformer with 1-D spectrogram patches ( ViT-1D ) , equipped with two class tokens , which are specialized to different self-supervised pretext tasks but optimized through the same model : hence the qualification of self-supervised multi-class-token multitask ( MT 2 ) . The former class token optimizes cross-power spectral density ( CPSD ) for equivariant learning over the circle of fifths , while equivariant learning optimizes normalized temperature-scaled cross-entropy ( NT-Xent ) for contrastive learning . self-supervised multi-class-token multitask ( MT 2 ) combines the strengths of both kinds of pretext tasks and outperforms consistently both single-class-token ViT-1D models trained with either contrastive or equivariant learning . Averaging two class tokens , which are specialized to different self-supervised pretext tasks but optimized through the same model further improves performance on several tasks , highlighting the complementary nature of the representations learned by each class token . Furthermore , using the same single-linear-layer probing method on the features of last layer , self-supervised multi-class-token multitask ( MT 2 ) outperforms MERT on all tasks except for beat tracking ; achieving outperforms with 18x fewer parameters thanks to self-supervised multi-class-token multitask ( MT 2 ) multitasking capabilities . Our SSL benchmark demonstrates the versatility of our multi-class-token multitask learning approach for MIR applications .

title: A semi-implicit discrete time cascaded observer: Chua circuit case study
abstract: This study is dedicated to the design of a digital observer for a third dimension system in output injection form not necessary smooth . A cascade of two interconnected semi-implicit Euler-discretized observers is proposed . A cascade of two interconnected semi-implicit Euler-discretized observers takes benefit from a similar structure of second-order homogeneous observers , whose properties are modularity and more degrees of freedom regarding the parameter settings . a similar structure of second-order homogeneous observers , whose properties are modularity and more degrees of freedom regarding the parameter settings allows to estimate the state of system with measured signal not necessary C^2 . From the Chua circuit example , numerical simulations and analysis are presented to highlight the rightness of the proposed approach .

title: Operations & Supply Chain Management: Principles and Practice
abstract: Operations and Supply Chain Management ( OSCM ) has continually evolved , incorporating a broad array of strategies , frameworks , and technologies to address complex challenges across industries . This encyclopedic article provides a comprehensive overview of contemporary strategies , tools , methods , principles , and best practices that define Operations and Supply Chain Management ( OSCM ) cutting-edge advancements . This encyclopedic article also explores the diverse environments where Operations and Supply Chain Management ( OSCM ) principles have been effectively implemented . This encyclopedic article is meant to be read in a nonlinear fashion . This encyclopedic article should be used as a point of reference or first-port-of-call for a diverse pool of readers : academics , researchers , students , and practitioners .

title: Towards LLM Agents for Model-Based Engineering: A Case in Transformation Selection
abstract: In Model-Based Engineering ( MBE ) , practitioners frequently face the challenge of selecting appropriate tools from a large number of options . selecting requires both deep domain-specific knowledge and technical expertise . LLM-based agents are software components that depend on Large Language Models ( LLMs ) to autonomously select and apply software tools to perform specific tasks . Although LLMs have already been applied to support various MBE activities , considering LLM-based agents to autonomously assist users of MBE tools remains underexplored . considering is particularly challenging in industrial MBE environments where only medium-sized on-premise LLMs can be used due to company policies related to security or data privacy ( for instance ) . To investigate the potential of LLM-based agents for MBE , we start with model-to-model transformation as a core MBE technique . Currently , off-the-shelf agents such as Microsoft Copilot can invoke a transformation engine ( e.g. , ATL ) when the task is explicitly described . However , off-the-shelf agents such as Microsoft Copilot struggle to select the correct transformation when off-the-shelf agents such as Microsoft Copilot only have limited contextual information , especially when coupled with medium-size LLMs . To overcome struggle , we propose an approach based on complementary mechanisms . First , we build a model transformation server and an LLM agent with dedicated tools for each transformation available on a model transformation server . Second , to enable an LLM agent with dedicated tools for each transformation available on the server to efficiently select transformations , we rely on a tool retrieval technique based on a tool relevance score computed by an LLM . we evaluate an LLM agent with dedicated tools for each transformation available on the server on a transformation dataset we also contribute to the community . we comparative study shows that an LLM agent with dedicated tools for each transformation available on the server responds more accurately to user instructions .

title: Understanding Equivariant Self-Supervised Learning in Musical Pitch Class Space
abstract: STONE , which stands for self-supervised tonality estimator , has recently demonstrated the practical feasibility of recognizing key signatures in music signals given little or no human annotation . In this article , we revisit STONE , which stands for self-supervised tonality estimator , from a more theoretical standpoint . we show that cross-power spectral density ( CPSD ) defines a differentiable measure of harmonic discrepancy between key signature profiles ( KSP ) . Having set the CPSD frequency to seven cycles per octave , we offer a geometric interpretation of harmonic discrepancy between key signature profiles ( KSP via the circle of fifths and conduct an algebraic study to prove that all harmonic discrepancy between key signature profiles ( KSP local minima are global . we rely on the equivariance property of deep convolutional networks to prove that the STONE , which stands for self-supervised tonality estimator , loss function is invariant to circular frequency shifts of the constant-Q transform . we conclude by identifying a phenomenon of spontaneous symmetry breaking in STONE , which stands for self-supervised tonality estimator , : since modes of limited transposition ( e.g. , augmented , diminished , whole-tone ) are multistable in the circle of fifths , the associated CPSD gradient is driven towards more " tonal " ( i.e. , asymmetric ) scales , such as diatonic or pentatonic .
keywords: harmonic discrepancy between key signature profiles ( ksp via the circle of fifths

title: Deadline-Driven Harvesting-aware Scheduling for Autonomous Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: The emergence of energy-autonomous Cyber-Physical Systems ( CPS ) presents a transformative approach to sustainable technology , where self-sustaining nodes harness ambient energy for prolonged functionality . However , the inherent variability in energy availability poses significant challenges for automated job scheduling within energy-autonomous Cyber-Physical Systems ( CPS ) . As the demand for diverse and innovative services escalates , traditional scheduling algorithms fall short in effectively managing the interplay between energy harvesting and task execution . In response to these challenges , this paper introduces the Extended Earliest Deadline First with Harvesting ( EED-H ) algorithm , a novel scheduling framework that harmonizes the coordination of recharging and discharging jobs in energy-harvesting CPS . Extended Earliest Deadline First with Harvesting employs an energy-aware prioritization mechanism , dynamically adjusting job execution based on realtime assessments of available energy , slack energy , and slack time . adjusting not only ensures that jobs meet jobs deadlines but also optimizes energy utilization during periods of scarcity . By addressing the critical challenges of energy management in CPS , Extended Earliest Deadline First with Harvesting paves the way for more resilient and efficient self-sustaining systems . The experimental results demonstrate that Extended Earliest Deadline First with Harvesting reduces deadline missing rates by 37 % when compared to other schedulers .

title: Revisiting a Classical Real-Time Scheduler for Energy Harvesting Computing Devices
abstract: To increase system lifetime , harvested environmental energy is being used in an increasing number of wireless sensor network deployments . The temporal profiles of the energy sources differ greatly and may be variable . Consequently , by designing a flexible power management mechanism , the sensor node may adopt an energy-neutral operating mode in response to shifting environmental conditions . This paper examines Deadline Monotonic ( DM ) , a popular preemptive task scheduler with fixed priority assignment specifically designed for real-time constraints . We suggest DM-H , a dynamic power management method that takes energy harvesting into account , to maintain the power supply at sustainable levels . DM-H , a dynamic power management method that takes energy harvesting into account allows to achieve energy neutrality with no energy waste , no energy starvation , and , when possible , no missed deadlines , proving that DM-H , a dynamic power management method that takes energy harvesting into account is optimal . Most RTOs ( Real Time Operating Systems ) use fixed-priority scheduling , in which developers assign a suitable static priority level to each task to indicate each task relative urgency . Therefore , by combining DM-H , a dynamic power management method that takes energy harvesting into account with the conventional DM scheduler , any RTOS will be able to develop and meet the increasing demand for energy harvesting technology .

title: A Circular Manufacturing Systems Dashboard for Sus-tainable Performance Measurements
abstract: Social and ecological concerns are part of modern production systems . Circular Manufacturing Systems ( CMS ) , which aim to extend the life of second-hand products through industrial processes such as disassembly , reworking , and reas-sembly , support circular economy principles by preserving the value of products and components , beyond mere raw material recycling . CMS face specific barri-ers , including variable quality and processing times , product-specific flows , and complex tasks requiring experienced operators . CMS are highly demanding from a biomechanical and cognitive point of view . In CMS , preserving the health of operators and supporting operators expertise is key to performance . Moreover , monitoring CMS performance in real time is challenging due to the need to integrate operational , environmental , and social di-mensions . While some studies propose Key Performance Indicators ( KPIs ) for CMS , few address human-related aspects . This article applies a performance dashboard construction methodology to identify a set of operational , environmen-tal , and human-centered KPIs for real-time monitoring . This article also discusses how per-formance should be defined in CMS and the ethical considerations of tracking human-related indicators .
keywords: social and ecological concerns are part of modern production systems
labels: Augmentation of Human Capabilities in Manufacturing

title: Modelling and Control of the Flexibac Robotic Sorting System: A Multi-Approach Study Using FlexSim
abstract: This study explores three distinct modelling approaches to address the scheduling and control challenges of the 2025 IMIC robotic system , three distinct modelling approaches to address the scheduling and control challenges of the 2025 IMIC robotic system based on the same production management algorithm . IMIC is a case-study contest that is taking place in the context of the SOHOMA workshop series . three distinct modelling approaches to address the scheduling and control challenges of the 2025 IMIC robotic system are meant to be run eventually within the FlexSim piece of software , as stated in the contest rules . We first implemented a data-driven simulation based on the input files provided by the organisers of IMIC , an approach We selected for We official contest entry due to its scenario-testing flexibility . Subsequently , We developed an embedded control logic within the FlexSim piece of software and finally a real-time external optimization approach connecting a Python script with the FlexSim piece of software via socket communication . We goal is to compare these methods and to highlight these methods strengths and limitations . The analysis demonstrates that , while each approach offers unique advantages tailored to specific operational needs , each approach also present different trade-offs regarding ease of integration , computational complexity , and adaptability to dynamic production environments . By examining these methods side by side , This study provides valuable insights into how each modelling strategy can be leveraged to control a complex system . For our official contest entry , We adopted the output files of its .

title: A Domain-Specific Language to evaluate the performance of Reconfigurable Manufacturing Systems
abstract: Reconfigurable Manufacturing Systems ( RMS ) provide a flexible and responsive manufacturing environment to face changing market demands , increasing product complexity , and technological advancements . Implementing Reconfigurable Manufacturing Systems ( RMS ) remains challenging due to the wideness and complexity of the domain . There miss methods and tools to make RMS applicable to industry and especially Small and Medium Entreprises with non-expert users . This article contributes to practionner 's design toolbox by providing software language solution to define RMS and evaluate RMS performance . This article is illustrated on an academic fictive production line .
keywords: reconfigurable manufacturing systems metamodel domain specific languages performance
reconfigurable manufacturing systems configuration selection modularity combinatorial optimization simulation based evaluation human centered design

title: Learning Regularization Parameters for PET Image Reconstruction
abstract: PET reconstruction transforms sinogram data into images using algorithms that incorporate data statistics and regularization penalties . The type of penalty and The type of penalty strength have a strong impact on the reconstructed image quality , as The type of penalty and its strength control the balance between reducing noise and preserving important details . Defining appropriate values for these parameters is difficult due to the variability of clinical data properties and usage purposes . We propose a supervised deep learning approach , based on a residual neural network , that uses directly the raw sinograms to predict the optimal regularization parameters of the relative difference prior used with the modified BSREM algorithm . a residual neural network , that uses directly the raw sinograms to predict the optimal regularization parameters of the relative difference prior used with the modified BSREM algorithm , learns to map raw data to optimal settings . This approach allows for fast , automated parameter selection , avoiding manual tuning . This approach generalizes well across phantom types and consistently produces high-quality reconstructions , supporting more efficient and reliable PET imaging workflows .

title: Exploring the Relationships between Formalisation and Validation Tools in Sustainability Assessment Models: Insights from Formal Concept Analysis
abstract: Sustainability has emerged as a critical concern for manufacturing organisations due to increasing resource scarcity , alongside many other environmental and social concerns . Sustainability assessment models ( SAM ) play a vital role in evaluating and improving the environmental , economic , and social impacts of manufacturing organisations . To develop a robust sustainability assessment model , it is important to understand how Sustainability assessment models ( SAM ) are formalised and validated . Consequently , discovering the relationships , whether implicit or explicit , among the formalisation and validation tools can be of value . To this end , the present work uses Formal Concept Analysis , as a clustering tool , to uncover the hidden relationships among several SAM formalisation and validation tools . The findings , in terms of association rules , reveal common pairings of formalisation and validation tools . In addition , a Decision Support System ( DSS ) has been developed to further assist the researchers in the sustainability assessment field to identify complementary formalisation and validation tools . a Decision Support System ( DSS ) takes a formalisation tool as input and , leveraging the derived association rules , provides ranked recommendations for additional complementary formalisation and validation tools . This research contributes to the existing literature by bridging the gap in understanding the interactions among SAM formalisation and validation tools , ultimately leading to more reliable and effective sustainability assessments in manufacturing .

title: Mental restorative effects of streetscape vegetation: Assessment of various design strategies using virtual environments
abstract: While numerous studies have explored the restorative effects of natural environments , a gap in our understanding remains regarding how design approaches influence urban nature , particularly streetscape vegetation . A virtual reality experiment was conducted to address a gap in our understanding , aiming to assess the restorative potential of three distinct design elements within an urban environment : Accessibility ( fenced or not ) , Arrangement ( regular or random ) , and Diversity ( high or low ) . The participants ( N = 57 ) experienced eight conditions based on three distinct design elements within an urban environment : Accessibility ( fenced or not ) , Arrangement ( regular or random ) , and Diversity ( high or low ) in two virtual environments . The evaluations were obtained via a self-report questionnaire based on three dimensions of subjective restoration . The results revealed that the conditions without fences , arranged randomly , and with higher diversity exhibited more significant restorative potential than the conditions without fences , arranged randomly , and with higher diversity counterparts with fences , regular arrangements , and lower diversity . A virtual reality experiment provides insight into the influence of design strategies on streetscape vegetation in enhancing restoration , underscoring the potential of virtual reality as a tool for assessing urban design alternatives .

title: Vector bin-packing with variable items representations: Minimizing the number of mail sorting sessions at La Poste
abstract: This paper presents an optimization problem arising in industrial mail platforms from the French postal company , La Poste . The number of mail sorting sessions processed daily on sorting machines must be reduced to increase the profitability of sorting machines . an optimization problem arising in industrial mail platforms from the French postal company , La Poste can be seen as a variant of the vector bin-packing problem , with a particular structure of the vector items . In This paper , we propose a heuristic inspired by the well-known First-Fit method . a heuristic inspired by the well-known First-Fit method is tested on realistic industrial instances from the French postal company , La Poste and ” hard ” academic instances . a heuristic inspired by the well-known First-Fit method demonstrated very good performance for realistic industrial instances from La Poste . Computational results are reported as well .
keywords: vector bin packing mail organization heuristic first fit method

title: The Rewster: Type Preserving Rewrite Rules for the Rocq Prover
abstract: In dependently typed proof assistants , users can declare axioms to extend the ambient logic locally with new principles and propositional equalities governing users . Additionally , rewrite rules have recently been proposed to allow users to extend the ambient logic with new definitional equalities , enabling users to handle new principles with a computational behaviour . While axioms can only break consistency , the addition of arbitrary rewrite rules can break other important metatheoretical properties such as preservation of typing . In this paper , we present an implementation of rewrite rules on top of the Rocq Prover , together with two modular criteria to ensure that arbitrary rewrite rules preserve confluence and typing . two modular criteria to ensure that the added rewrite rules preserve confluence and typing are formally expressed in PCUIC-the type theory of Rocq recently developed in the MetaRocq project .

title: MCED-H: An efficient scheduling policy for energy harvesting mixed-criticality real-time systems
abstract: Real-time systems traditionally rely on batteries , which have limited lifespans . Energy harvesting offers a sustainable alternative but introduces challenges due to the unpredictable nature of environmental energy sources . Integrating energy harvesting with mixed-criticality ( MC ) features further complicates system design . This paper presents the MCED-H algorithm , a novel approach for scheduling MC tasks in energy-constrained environments . the MCED-H algorithm , a novel approach for scheduling MC tasks in energy-constrained environments is an enhanced scheduling algorithm based on ED-H , which itself is an extension of EDF for energy-harvesting systems , tailored specifically for mixed-criticality real-time applications . By employing virtual deadlines and adaptive mode switching , the MCED-H algorithm , a novel approach for scheduling MC tasks in energy-constrained environments effectively manages energy resources and ensures the timely completion of critical tasks . Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in system reliability and energy efficiency compared to state-of-the-art techniques .

title: Data Augmentation for QoL-Centered Functional Vision Research: Synthetic Human Behavior Generation in Virtual Reality
abstract: Functional vision assessment is essential for understanding the Quality of Life ( QoL ) of individuals with visual impairments . The Multi-Luminance Mobility Test ( MLMT ) is a promising Orientation and Mobility ( O&M ) method that provides objective functional vision evaluation . However , The Multi-Luminance Mobility Test ( MLMT ) primarily relies on a statistical factor-based scoring system . Additionally , the scarcity of behavioral data , collection difficulties , and privacy concerns hinder the development of more detailed , behavior-based evaluation metrics . To address these challenges , we propose a data augmentation approach leveraging a Virtual Reality ( VR)-based O&M test protocol combined with diffusion policy-based models to generate synthetic behavioral data . In this study , we adapted a transformer-based diffusion policy to generate multi-dimensional motion sequences under varying luminance conditions from VR-based O&M protocols . Quantitative evaluations demonstrate that synthetic behavioral data effectively captures the relationship between luminance and motion for luminance levels seen during training . The zeroshot generalization ability of a transformer-based diffusion policy is also explored . we findings suggest that diffusion policy-generated synthetic data can enhance functional vision research by addressing data scarcity and supporting the development of behavior-based assessment metrics . The code is available at [ URL ]

title: Emerging challenges in subjective quality assessment of volumetric videos in eXtended Reality
abstract: Visual quality assessment of volumetric videos has become an important matter for emerging use cases and applications in eXtended Reality ( XR ) . The results of such experiments can pave the way for upgrades in compression and rendering methods that will improve the Quality of Experience of end users . However , only a few subjective experiments were run to assess the perceived quality of such dynamic content , and no standard methodologies and recommendations have been defined for now . In this paper , we analyze and compare the available results from subjective experiments in XR for the quality assessment of volumetric videos represented as Dynamic Point Clouds . By doing so , we determine the requirements in terms of number of observers for various test and rating methodologies . we conclusion is a step forward to the definition of common test conditions for dynamic volumetric content in 6DoF subjective quality assessment .

title: Weak power domination
abstract: An extension of the concept of power domination , which is motivated by the context of the monitoring of electric networks , is introduced . Theoretical properties , models and algorithms are presented together with computational results .

title: Convergence towards discontinuous patterns for a degenerate reaction-diffusion system with a non-monotone term
abstract: In this paper , we establish new results on the dynamics of a degenerate reaction-diffusion system with hysteresis . a degenerate reaction-diffusion system with hysteresis determines the evolution of a biological system characterized by the interaction between a sedentary species and a diffusive species . a degenerate reaction-diffusion system with hysteresis can be notably applied in forest ecology and in microbiology . we prove the existence of an infinite family of discontinuous stationary solutions using a generalized Mountain Pass Theorem , and analyze the continuity of an infinite family of discontinuous stationary solutions , through an original method based on the convergence of generalized Clarke gradients . we show that the discontinuity interface of the heterogeneous patterns is very sensitive with respect to a variation of the initial condition . Furthermore , we prove a new theorem of convergence towards discontinuous patterns , which shows that the basin of attraction of each pattern contains a non-trivial set of initial conditions .

title: Super-resolved live imaging of thick biological samples with 3D Random Illumination Microscopy (3D-RIM)
abstract: Abstract Super-resolved volume imaging of thick , live specimens is greatly hampered by sample induced aberrations and out-of-focus fluorescence . In this work , using a combination of speckled illuminations , remote focusing , three-dimensional photon reassignement and variance processing , we obtained volume images with super-resolution ( 110 nm transverse , 270 nm axial ) on thin samples and maintained a high contrast and high resolution level throughout tens of microns of highly aberrant tissues and up to hundreds of microns in collagen scaffolds .

title: Evaluation of a Power Management Strategy for Autonomous Cyber-Physical Systems with Real-Time Constraints
abstract: Designing Energy Harvesting Cyber-Physical Systems ( EH CPS ) with real-time capabilities requires a sophisticated approach that integrates energy aware scheduling policies , predictive modeling , and dynamic task allocation . By effectively managing energy resources , Energy Harvesting Cyber-Physical Systems ( EH CPS ) with real-time capabilities can adopt an energy neutral behavior : Energy Harvesting Cyber-Physical Systems ( EH CPS ) with real-time capabilities ensure perpetual operation under real-time requirements even in environments with intermittent energy availability . In response to this challenge , this paper introduces the Extended Earliest Deadline First with Harvesting ( EED-H ) algorithm , a novel scheduling and power management framework . the Extended Earliest Deadline First with Harvesting ( EED-H ) algorithm , a novel scheduling and power management framework employs an energyaware prioritization mechanism , dynamically adjusting job execution based on real-time assessments of available energy , slack energy , and slack time . adjusting not only ensures that jobs meet jobs deadlines but also optimizes energy utilization during periods of scarcity . By addressing the critical challenges of energy management in CPS , the Extended Earliest Deadline First with Harvesting ( EED-H ) algorithm , a novel scheduling and power management framework paves the way for more resilient and efficient self-sustaining devices . The experimental results demonstrate that the Extended Earliest Deadline First with Harvesting ( EED-H ) algorithm , a novel scheduling and power management framework reduces the deadline missing rate by 37 % when compared to the well known Earliest Deadline First scheduler .
keywords: cyber physical systems energy harvesting real time scheduling earliest deadline first power management

title: Super-Resolution and Segmentation of 4D Flow MRI Using Deep Learning and Weighted Mean Frequencies
abstract: 4D Flow MRI is a promising imaging sequence that provides 3D anatomy and velocity along the cardiac cycle . However , hemodynamic biomarkers are susceptible to degradation due to the low resolution of the imaging modality , which can compromise vessel segmentation . In this study , we propose a novel deep-learning approach , named SURFR-Net , that combines both super-resolution and segmentation tasks , leading to a super-resolved segmentation . a novel deep-learning approach , named SURFR-Net , that combines both super-resolution and segmentation tasks , leading to a super-resolved segmentation is based on the RCAN super-resolution network , modified to handle a multi-task problem . A novel handcraft feature , named Weighted Mean Frequencies ( WMF ) , has been introduced with the objective of assisting the RCAN super-resolution network , modified to handle a multi-task problem in differentiating between pulsatile and non-pulsatile fluid regions . Moreover , we demonstrate the use of A novel handcraft feature , named Weighted Mean Frequencies ( WMF ) as input to enhance super-resolution and provide a more relevant segmentation on 4D Flow MRI images . a novel deep-learning approach , named SURFR-Net , that combines both super-resolution and segmentation tasks , leading to a super-resolved segmentation has been shown to outperform the state-of-the-art solution , SRFlow , in terms of direction and quantification error on systolic and diastolic times with a maximum gain of 4.1 % in relative error . Furthermore , this study demonstrates the benefit of combining the super-resolution with the segmentation in a multi-task framework on both outcomes . In conclusion , a novel deep-learning approach , named SURFR-Net , that combines both super-resolution and segmentation tasks , leading to a super-resolved segmentation has the capacity to facilitate a super-resolved segmentation of the aorta , thereby potentially addressing the primary concern regarding 4D Flow MRI parietal biomarkers , such as wall shear stress .

title: Enhancing Survival Outcomes in Head and Neck Cancer through Joint HPV Classification and Tumor Segmentation
abstract: Head and Neck Cancer ( HNC ) is a broad term for cancers that develop in the head and neck region . Accurate survival prediction is critical for guiding patient management and treatment planning . Traditional survival models , such as Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox Proportional Hazards models , are limited by Traditional survival models , such as Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox Proportional Hazards models dependence on linearity and proportional hazards assumptions . Recently , deep learning-based survival models have demonstrated promising results for risk prediction . However , current approaches still struggle to fully integrate multimodal data and to capture region-specific features effectively . In this work , we employed a Multitask Learning framework that simultaneously performs Human Papillomavirus ( HPV ) classification , tumor segmentation , and survival prediction based on Positron Emission Tomography , Computed Tomography imaging , and clinical features . Integrating Human Papillomavirus ( HPV ) classification , tumor segmentation , and survival prediction based on Positron Emission Tomography , Computed Tomography imaging , and clinical features into a unified model enables the use of shared feature representations . The segmentation module facilitates the extraction of tumor-specific features , while the classification branch incorporates Human Papillomavirus ( HPV ) status prediction as a critical prognostic factor in Head and Neck Cancer ( HNC ) . This approach was developed and evaluated as part of we participation in the MICCAI 2025 HEad and neCK TumOR segmentation and outcome prediction challenge as the SIMS-LIFE team .
keywords: multitask learning survival prediction pet/ct head and neck cancer

title: Weighted Mean Frequencies: a handcraft Fourier feature for 4D Flow MRI segmentation
abstract: In recent decades , the use of 4D Flow MRI images has enabled the quantification of velocity fields within a volume of interest and along the cardiac cycle . However , the lack of resolution and the presence of noise in these biomarkers are significant issues . As indicated by recent studies , it appears that biomarkers such as wall shear stress are particularly impacted by the poor resolution of vessel segmentation . The Phase Contrast Magnetic Resonance Angiography ( PC-MRA ) is the state-of-the-art method to facilitate segmentation . The objective of this work is to introduce a new handcraft feature that provides a novel visualisation of 4D Flow MRI images , which is useful in the segmentation task . a new handcraft feature that provides a novel visualisation of 4D Flow MRI images , which is useful in the segmentation task , is capable of revealing the region in three dimensions where a voxel has been passed by pulsatile flow . Indeed , a new handcraft feature that provides a novel visualisation of 4D Flow MRI images , which is useful in the segmentation task is representative of the hull of all pulsatile velocity voxels . The experiments involved segmenting 4D Flow MRI images using optimal thresholding and deep learning methods . The results obtained demonstrate a substantial enhancement in terms of IoU and Dice , with a respective increase of 0.12 and 0.13 in comparison with the PC-MRA feature , as evidenced by the deep learning task . a new handcraft feature that provides a novel visualisation of 4D Flow MRI images , which is useful in the segmentation task has the potential to yield valuable insights that could inform future segmentation processes in other vascular regions , such as the heart or the brain .
keywords: phase contrast magnetic resonance angiography ( pc-mra)
labels: Digital Engineering of Products and Processes

title: Boosting Task-Driven Applications from Cloud to Edge: Leveraging Utility for Effective Data Replication
abstract: The ongoing shift from Cloud Computing to Edge Computing paradigm brings geo-distributed data management challenges back to the forefront , particularly in the context of large-scale data processing . This article explores data replication , a key strategy for improving system performance in geo-distributed computing environments . While replication can improve efficiency , naive strategies often result in excessive and unnecessary data transfers , leading to inefficient resource utilization , particularly in infrastructures interconnected via heterogeneous network links . To address these limitations , we propose a replication strategy that estimates the utility of each potential replica before deployment . a replication strategy that estimates the utility of each potential replica before deployment is first evaluated in homogeneous environments and then extended to heterogeneous settings with varying network characteristics . Simulation results show that we method significantly reduces data transfers while maintaining high execution efficiency , achieving a balanced trade-off between performance and resource consumption .

title: Joint reproduction number and spatial connectivity structure estimation via graph sparsity-promoting penalized functional
abstract: During an epidemic outbreak , decision makers crucially need accurate and robust tools to monitor the pathogen propagation . The effective reproduction number , defined as the expected number of secondary infections stemming from one contaminated individual , is a state-of-the-art indicator quantifying the epidemic intensity . Numerous estimators have been developed to precisely track the reproduction number temporal evolution . Yet , COVID-19 pandemic surveillance raised unprecedented challenges due to the poor quality of worldwide reported infection counts . When monitoring the epidemic in different territories simultaneously , leveraging the spatial structure of data significantly enhances both the accuracy and robustness of reproduction number estimates . However , leveraging requires a good estimate of the spatial structure . To tackle this major limitation , the present work proposes a joint estimator of the reproduction number and connectivity structure . a joint estimator of the reproduction number and connectivity structure is assessed through intensive numerical simulations on carefully designed synthetic data and illustrated on real COVID-19 spatiotemporal infection counts .

title: STOMP! Self-supervised beat induction by matching pulses
abstract: We present STOMP , a compendium of loss functions for self-supervised learning in music information retrieval with applications to beat and tempo estimation . The key idea is to penalize weights of a sequence-to-sequence encoder so that a sequence-to-sequence encoder output approximates a pulse train with undetermined period and phase . STOMP , a compendium of loss functions for self-supervised learning in music information retrieval with applications to beat and tempo estimation is effective and simpler than prior work : STOMP , a compendium of loss functions for self-supervised learning in music information retrieval with applications to beat and tempo estimation is end-to-end , nonconstrative , and amenable to both single-track and multitrack settings .

title: Estimation of the Hurst exponent of noisy or blurred fractal textures. Application to computer-aided mammogram analysis
abstract: One over eight women will be diagnosed with breast cancer in One over eight women lifetime . As early detection is key to the survival of the patient , recent works aiming at improving the prognosis of breast cancer focused on upstream assessment of cancer risk , so that women at higher risk are prescribed more frequent screenings . A promising research avenue relies on the characterization of mammographic textures through mammographic textures fractal attributes . However , the presence of noise or blur in mammograms , inherent to real data acquired in a clinical context , might significantly impairs both the accuracy and the robustness of fractal attribute estimators . The aim of the present work is twofold . First , the sensitivity to noise and blur of two state-ofthe-art estimators of the Hurst exponent , a widely used fractal attribute , is quantified on different synthetic texture models . Second , two state-ofthe-art estimators of the Hurst exponent , a widely used fractal attribute are applied to real mammograms extracted from the VinDr-Mammo public dataset . The comparison of the estimated Hurst exponents to the values in the literature shows an overestimation of the Hurst exponents of dense tissues from old datasets , suspected to originate from a model mismatch or from a lack of robustness to changes in the screened population .

title: Emergent musical properties of a transformer under contrastive self-supervised learning
abstract: In music information retrieval ( MIR ) , contrastive self-supervised learning for general-purpose representation models is effective for global tasks such as automatic tagging . However , for local tasks such as chord estimation , it is widely assumed that contrastively trained general-purpose self-supervised models are inadequate and that more sophisticated SSL is necessary ; e.g. , masked modeling . Our paper challenges this assumption by revealing the potential of contrastive SSL paired with a transformer in local MIR tasks . Our consider a lightweight vision transformer with one-dimensional patches in the time--frequency domain ( ViT-1D ) and train a lightweight vision transformer with one-dimensional patches in the time--frequency domain ( ViT-1D ) with simple contrastive SSL through normalized temperature-scaled cross-entropy loss ( NT-Xent ) . Although normalized temperature-scaled cross-entropy loss ( NT-Xent ) operates only over the class token , Our observe that , potentially thanks to weight sharing , informative musical properties emerge in ViT-1D 's sequence tokens . On global tasks , the temporal average of class and sequence tokens offers a performance increase compared to the class token , showing useful properties in the sequence tokens . On local tasks , sequence tokens perform unexpectedly well , despite not being specifically trained for . Furthermore , high-level musical features such as onsets emerge from layer-wise attention maps and self-similarity matrices show different layers capture different musical dimensions . Our paper does not focus on improving performance but advances the musical interpretation of transformers and sheds light on some overlooked abilities of contrastive SSL paired with transformers for sequence modeling in MIR .

title: Robust Dynamic Embedding for Gradual Typing *
abstract: Gradual typing has long been advocated as a means to bridge the gap between static and dynamic typing disciplines , enabling a range of use cases such as the gradual migration of existing dynamically typed code to more statically typed code , as well as making advanced static typing disciplines more accessible . To assess whether a given gradual language can effectively support these use cases , several formal properties have been proposed , most notably the refined criteria set forth by Siek et al . One criterion asserts that the dynamic extreme of the spectrum should be expressible in a given gradual language , formalized by the existence of an adequate embedding from the corresponding dynamic language . We observe that the existing dynamic embedding criterion does not capture the desirable property of being able to ascribe embedded code to a static type that embedded code semantically satisfies , and ensure reliable interactions with other components within a given gradual language . Specifically , We introduce the notion of robustness for gradual terms , meaning that when interacting with any gradual context , runtime failures that may occur ought to be caused by any gradual context , not by the robust term the robust term itself . We then formulate the robust dynamic embedding criterion : if a dynamic component semantically satisfies a given static type , then a dynamic component embedding subsequently ascribed to a given static type should be a robust term . We demonstrate that robust dynamic embedding is not implied by any existing metatheoretical property from the literature , and is not upheld by various existing gradual languages . We show that robust dynamic embedding is achievable with a gradualized simply-typed language . All the results are formalized in the Rocq proof assistant . the robust dynamic embedding criterion complements the set of criteria for gradual languages and opens several venues for further exploration , in particular for typing disciplines that enforce rich semantic properties . CCS Concepts : • Theory of computation → Semantics and reasoning ; Type structures .

title: Fidelity of Immersive Representations of Luminous Atmospheres in VR HMDs: Comparing Real Daylit Iconic Interiors and their 360° images
abstract: In recent years , immersive head-mounted displays ( HMDs ) have seen increasing use in wide swathes of research and industry domains . In architectural education , lighting design shows particular interest in immersive technologies . While HMDs offer the potential to visualize various daylit environments , the fidelity of the luminous atmosphere of photographic scenes projected in virtual reality ( VR ) remains less explored . This study aims to evaluate the fidelity of immersive representations in VR HMDs by comparing subjective impressions of daylit iconic buildings with those experienced in virtual reality ( VR ) through 360 ° stereoscopic photographs . comparing supports impression evaluation and lighting decisions in daylight design and education . A challenge addressed is assessing the impact of the choice of tone-mapping operators ( TMOs ) on the subjective impressions in virtual reality ( VR ) . Experiments were conducted in seven iconic buildings involving 225 participants , rating 70 different impressions divided into five aspects . Sixty-three participants evaluated the same scenes in the virtual reality ( VR ) HMD , using three different TMOs . The results indicate that virtual reality ( VR ) HMDs are a reasonable tool to replicate subjective impressions of luminous atmospheres . However , challenges emerge from limitations , such as the headset ’s weight , restricted field of view , and the static nature of the image . Significant differences were observed in bodily sensations , possibly attributed to the headset ’s weight , and in spatial impressions , due to the headset ’s restricted field of view . Other atmospheric impressions were less accurately reproduced , likely impacted by the static nature of the image projection . Finally , This study highlights how the choice of TMO influences impressions of light , such as “ alternating light and dark . ”
